newsitem.title: USA: Tech stock travails continue to drag down Nasdaq.
newsitem.headline: Tech stock travails continue to drag down Nasdaq.

text.p: Flagging blue chip technology stocks tugged down the broad market on Friday, continuing a three-week slide in the sector, which has been spurred on by fears of slowing profits especially in the networking sector.

The Nasdaq Composite fell 13.09 points to 1334.32, or about one percent, spurred on by strong selling pressure in Cisco Systems Inc and Intel Corp, which fell 4-5/8 points to 53-3/8 and 3-1/2 to 146-3/8, respectively.
"Tech stocks particularly the networkers, the semiconductors and the PC makers were hit the hardest," one trader said as decliners edged out advancers 2259 to 2056.

The trader said the sell-off was triggered by comments from a Soundview analyst who argued that PC makers gross margins have peaked. "After that, anything computer related got hit, with networkers taking it the hardest," he said.
Cascade Communications Corp continued a month long plummet, joined by 3Com Corp and Cisco, hit by fears over near-term earnings prospects, analysts said.

Scholastic Corp shares tumbled 24-3/4 points to 36-3/4, or almost 41 percent, after it surprised investors on Thursday with its expectation of a fiscal third quarter loss and decline in earnings for the fiscal year ending in May.
